assumptions: USD million; 365-day convention. Toy operating working capital metrics exclude financing balances and advances for fixed assets. Average of opening/closing values used; sales all credit, purchase denominator supplied.

evidence.text: [Balance] Trade AR 120→150; inventory 100→140; trade AP 80→90. Supplier-finance debt 30→70; equipment advances 10→50. All balances separate.
[P&L] Credit sales 900, COGS 600; credit inventory purchases 640. No seasonality correction or writeoffs.
[Definition] DSO=avg trade AR/credit sales×365; DIO=avg inventory/COGS×365; DPO=avg trade AP/credit inventory purchases×365.
[Management] Analyst adds supplier-finance debt to AP to show improved operating DPO; uses sales rather than purchases for DPO in another slide.
[Cash] CFO 120, cash capex 80, no supplier financing payment detail.

qas.question: Find DSO under the stipulated credit-sales denominator.
Find inventory days using the average inventory balance.
Calculate operating DPO excluding supplier financing.
Find the toy operating cash conversion cycle.
Why is adding supplier-finance debt to operating AP misleading here?
qas.answer: The definition excludes financing; including it makes payment days appear longer through borrowing rather than trade terms.

qas.question: Should equipment advances enter inventory days?
qas.answer: No. They relate to fixed assets, not the defined operating inventory.

qas.question: Can an exact supplier-finance-adjusted CFO be computed from the debt balance increase?
qas.answer: No. Noncash transfers, principal payments and classifications are not disclosed.

qas.question: Does the year-end inventory balance prove inventory inefficiency throughout the year?
qas.answer: No. Two snapshots cannot identify seasonality or stock-out protection; operational data are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy gross margin decomposition uses prior channel margin at current channel sales for mix, then changes in channel margin. Sales net of returns. No other channels.

evidence.text:
[Channel statement]
| Channel | Prior sales | Prior GP | Current sales | Current GP |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stores | 600 | 240 | 500 | 195 |
| Online | 400 | 100 | 600 | 144 |
[Current online note] Gross billed online 650, returns/discounts 50; online GP 144 already after deductions and related COGS. No further reduction.
[Bridge convention] First hold prior margins at current net sales mix, then apply actual current margins. All percentages use total net sales.
[Central costs] Current opex 300, prior opex 280; no tax or interest.
[Memo] CEO attributes total gross margin decline entirely to higher return rate; prior return data absent.

qas.question: Find prior aggregate gross margin.
Find current aggregate gross margin.
Find counterfactual current gross profit at prior channel margins.
Quantify mix-only change in aggregate gross margin, in percentage points.
Quantify within-channel margin effect in percentage points at current weights.
Explain why subtracting online returns 50 from current net sales again is incorrect.
qas.answer: The 600 online net sales already reflect the 50 reduction; repeating it double-counts returns.

qas.question: Can the return-rate effect be isolated from the within-channel margin change?
qas.answer: No. Prior returns, discount and cost effects are not separately disclosed.

qas.question: Is higher online sales share necessarily a worse long-term business decision?
qas.answer: Not established; channel gross margin alone omits growth economics, customer costs and investment needs.

assumptions: USD million. Toy reported cost/income ratio uses operating expenses divided by NII + fee income + trading result + disposal gain; adjusted excludes disposal gain and verified one-time integration expense. Credit losses outside ratio.

evidence.text: [P&L] NII 300, fee income 90, trading gain 20, disposal gain 40. Operating expenses 220 including integration expense 15; impairment charge 60.
[Policy] Reported ratio uses all four income items and operating expenses. Adjusted ratio removes disposal gain 40 and integration expense 15 only.
[Prior year] Adjusted income 390, adjusted operating expenses 195. Same definition.
[Cash] Disposal gain 40 arose from sale proceeds 100 and carrying amount 60. No other cash data.
[Presentation] Analyst divides expenses plus credit losses by revenue excluding disposal and calls it management adjusted ratio.

qas.question: Find reported operating income denominator.
Calculate reported cost/income ratio.
Calculate management adjusted cost/income ratio under its stated policy.
Find change in adjusted cost/income ratio versus prior year in pp.
Why does excluding a gain raise the ratio even when expense is also reduced?
qas.answer: Income falls proportionately more than adjusted expense in this case; reported and adjusted bases differ.

qas.question: Does the 100m sale cash belong in the ratio denominator?
qas.answer: No. The reported income includes the 40m gain, not gross disposal cash.

qas.question: Can integration expense 15 be independently verified as one-time?
qas.answer: No. The policy labels it but there is no recurrence history or underlying expense detail.

qas.question: Can a regulatory efficiency benchmark be determined from these ratios?
qas.answer: No. No external comparison or standardized regulatory definition is given.

assumptions: USD million. Toy organic constant-currency growth compares continuing book, excludes acquired book and adjusts current foreign revenue at prior FX. Gross written premium, not earned.

evidence.text: [2024] Domestic written premium 300 USD; foreign 200 EUR translated at 1.10 USD/EUR. No acquired book.
[2025] Domestic continuing written premium 330 USD; foreign continuing 220 EUR; acquired book written premium 80 USD. Current average FX 1.25 USD/EUR.
[Earned note] Total 2025 earned premium 625 USD, includes unearned movements, not a written growth denominator.
[Policy] Organic excludes acquisition 80; constant currency uses 1.10 for foreign continuing 2025. No disposals.
[Deck] Headline says total growth from 520 to 685 equals organic growth.

qas.question: Find reported 2024 gross written premium in USD.
Find reported 2025 written premium including acquisition.
Find continuing 2025 written premium at prior FX.
Find organic constant-currency written premium growth.
Explain the dollar bridge from 520 to 685.
qas.answer: Underlying growth 52; currency 33; acquisition 80; total increase 165.

qas.question: Why not use 625 earned premium in the written growth bridge?
qas.answer: It is a distinct coverage-recognition metric; growth requires consistent written-premium scope.

qas.question: Can acquisition's contribution to underwriting profit be quantified?
qas.answer: No. Acquired earned premium, claims and expense are missing.

qas.question: Can organic growth be separated into policy count and pricing?
qas.answer: No. Written premium aggregates both; counts and rate changes are absent.

assumptions: USD million. Toy Rule of 40 = YoY recognized revenue growth + FCF margin. FCF deducts both equipment and capitalized development; no other adjustment. Annual values only.

evidence.text: [P&L] Prior annual revenue 400, current annual revenue 500. Current operating profit 30 includes SBC 45.
[Cash] CFO 100, equipment capex 20, capitalized development 30, acquisition cash 60. Toy FCF excludes acquisitions but deducts both recurring capital spend categories.
[Dashboard] ARR growth 35%; management slide calculates Rule of 40 using ARR growth plus adjusted operating margin excluding SBC.
[Policy] The requested metric uses recognized revenue growth and stated FCF margin. No future forecast.
[Investor note] FCF 50 still includes working-capital effects and cash taxes; no breakdown supplied.

qas.question: Find annual recognized revenue growth for the stated Rule of 40.
Find free cash flow under the stated capital spending convention.
qas.answer: 100−20−30=50 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate the defined FCF margin.
Calculate the requested Rule of 40 score.
qas.answer: 25+10=35 percentage points.

qas.question: Why is the management slide's ARR-based score not comparable to the requested score?
qas.answer: ARR growth and adjusted operating margin measure different bases from recognized revenue growth and FCF margin.

qas.question: Should acquisition cash 60 be deducted for the stated FCF metric?
qas.answer: No. The specified definition excludes acquisitions, though they consume real cash.

qas.question: Does FCF margin 10% establish durable recurring cash profitability?
qas.answer: No. Working-capital timing, tax and capital spending may vary; breakdown and history are missing.

qas.question: Can cash flow excluding stock-based compensation's economic dilution be calculated?
qas.answer: No. SBC expense alone does not determine dilution or repurchase cash requirements.

assumptions: USD million; thousand MWh. Toy levelized cost is PV of lifecycle costs divided by PV of delivered MWh. Operating cash cost uses current-year cash only. Supplied PV quantities already discounted.

evidence.text: [Lifecycle model] Discounted construction cost 180m, discounted operating/maintenance 90m, decommissioning PV 10m, salvage PV 5m. Discounted delivered generation 5,000k MWh.

[Presentation] Manager calls current cash opex divided by output LCOE and adds interest 5m to lifecycle costs.

qas.question: Find net discounted lifetime project cost.
Find stipulated LCOE in USD per delivered MWh.
Find current operating cash cost per MWh.
Find LCOE in the lower-output sensitivity.
Why is current operating cash cost not LCOE?
qas.answer: It excludes upfront and end-of-life costs and measures only one year's output.

qas.question: Should the 5m current interest be added to discounted lifecycle costs?
qas.answer: Not under the toy discount convention; financing interest is excluded by definition.

qas.question: Does LCOE below realized tariff prove positive project NPV?
qas.answer: Not necessarily. Timing and future realized tariffs/cash flows are absent.

qas.question: Can LCOE be recalculated with a different discount rate?
qas.answer: No. Undiscounted dated costs and generation series are missing.

assumptions: USD million; million units. Toy common NAV subtracts liabilities and preferred claim from assets. Market capitalization uses common units only; price discount uses common NAV per unit.

qas.question: Find total net assets before allocation to preferred and common.
Find NAV attributable to common units.
qas.answer: 450−100=350 million USD.

qas.question: Calculate common NAV per unit.
Find common market price discount to common NAV, expressed as positive percentage.

qas.answer: Preferred holders have a separate 100m claim; it is not attributable to common units.

qas.question: Does a discount to NAV necessarily indicate undervaluation?
qas.answer: No. Asset valuation uncertainty, governance, liquidity and risk can explain it.

qas.question: Can enterprise value including market value of preferred be calculated exactly?
qas.answer: No. Preferred market value and debt market value are absent.

qas.question: Can total distributions for both equity classes be determined?

assumptions: USD million. Toy subperiod time-weighted return compounds returns excluding external flow. Subscription occurs exactly between subperiods, no distributions. Do not treat full NAV increase as return.

evidence.text: [Valuation] Start NAV 100m. Immediately before midyear subscription NAV 110m. Investor contributes 50m; immediately after flow NAV 160m.
[Year-end] NAV 152m. No other subscriptions, withdrawals or distributions.
[Definition] Subperiod return before flow =110/100−1; after flow =152/160−1. Multiply growth factors for TWR.
[Deck] Sales claims 52% annual investment return because NAV grew from 100 to 152.
[Investor data] Existing investors' unit counts unchanged; no individual contribution dates other than stated aggregate subscription.

qas.question: Find first-half portfolio return before the subscription.
Find second-half portfolio return after external capital.
Find compounded time-weighted return for the year.
Find dollar net investment result after removing external subscription.
qas.answer: 152−100−50=2 million USD.

qas.question: Why does a positive time-weighted return coexist with only 2m dollar gain?
qas.answer: The larger asset base after subscription suffered a loss of 8m, offsetting the earlier 10m gain; TWR weights subperiod rates, not capital size.

qas.question: Why is the claimed 52% not an investment performance measure?
qas.answer: It includes contributed capital 50m, not just investment returns.

qas.question: Can the new subscriber's after-tax personal return be found?
qas.answer: No. Tax, fees or investor-specific terms are missing.

qas.question: Can daily return volatility be computed from the two subperiod valuations?
qas.answer: No. Daily NAV and flow series are absent.
